summary: I pass on all three markets. But the books' own de-vigged number for MIL is 0.5535, and that already reflects most of the starter and team-quality gap, so I do not see what the price misses. King's FIP of 4.1311 and recent ERA of 5.2941 lean toward MIL, but Henderson has only 98.33 innings this year. Lineups are not posted, and there is no matchup history or standings snapshot, so any lean rests on thin ground. On the run line, SD +1.5 at -185 is too expensive to chase, and MIL -1.5 at +165 needs a bigger win than the evidence supports. The total of 7 is priced almost level, with the over at 0.5092 fair probability, a retractable roof and a wind of 11.9 mph that I cannot read without knowing the roof status. The market is probably right on all three.

Blake Snell has a 1.8984 ERA and a 1.8564 FIP, and the Dodgers have won 8 of their last 10, but the Braves starter Ray Kerr has almost no sample in the data, so we cannot say the market is wrong about either arm. The run line and the total are near coin flips, with fair probabilities of 0.5206 for ATL +1.5 and 0.5109 for Under 8, and the hot, dry forecast works against a low-scoring read. The player props are thin. Most are quoted by only two or three books, those quotes are far older than the lineups, and Max Muncy and Ha-Seong Kim do not appear in either posted lineup. The Drake Baldwin hits prop is the closest call, since LineHound's own model likes the over, but Snell is a hard matchup and a 29-game sample is small.
